Start group-kill test timeout once its child is ready (TODO 253) (#282)

TODO 253 records 1 run of tools/test-skill-release-date-client.py
that errored with FileNotFoundError for sleeper.pid in
test_a_child_that_does_not_end_is_killed_with_its_group, and 3 reruns
that passed. That is the TODO's record, not a check of this change.

The sleeper, its pid file and the probe of its pid with os.kill are
removed. The stub child now forks 1 member into its group and then
writes 1 byte to a FIFO, alive, and the client's first wait starts
only once the test reads that byte, polled for at most 60 seconds; the
poll is new to this test. The test asserts the client's reason first,
then that the byte was read when the poll ended, that the client asked
its first wait for exactly its 1 second timeout, that the real wait
lasted at least that long, and that the client's run, from its start
to its return, less the poll, ended within 15 seconds; main bounds the
whole run by 15 seconds.

End of file on alive within 10 seconds after the client returns shows
that the client killed the whole group, not only the leader: it comes
only once every process holding the write end has ended. Its time is a
clock read taken after the read that sees it, and a time past that
deadline counts as not seen. Each stub process otherwise ends by
itself 90 seconds after it enters its wait for the release, and so
more than 90 seconds after the test's start. The check takes no end of
file seen later than 85 seconds from that start, the 60 second poll,
the 15 second run and the 10 second check, plus the poll's last step,
and end of file must come before 90 seconds, so the group's own end is
never taken for the kill.

The test sends no signal. Each stub process waits for end of file on
a second FIFO, lifeline, whose only write end the test holds. The
check's finally clause closes lifeline and reaps a child the client
left unreaped if it ends within the 5 second reap grace, and the
kernel closes lifeline when the test process ends in any other way.
The stub makes 1 read of lifeline before it forks. On Linux, select
reports nothing for a FIFO reader opened with no writer, and that read
returns end of file, so a stub that starts after the release exits at
once rather than wait out its 90 seconds. A stub process past that
read ends at once on the release; one not yet there ends when it
reaches it, after the rest of its start-up, which the test does not
bound.

The stub's source ignores SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP, and Python
ignores SIGPIPE and SIGXFSZ at start-up. The stub keeps every signal
that the test thread that starts it blocks as blocked, and every
signal other than SIGCHLD, SIGPIPE and SIGXFSZ that the test process
ignores as ignored. The client changes those 3 dispositions before
exec: it resets SIGCHLD to its default in its own process, the test
process, before it starts the child, and its Popen, with its default
restore_signals, resets SIGPIPE and SIGXFSZ to their default action
in the child. SIGCHLD's default action, like ignoring it, leaves the
stub running. So, unless the test thread blocks it, SIGPIPE or SIGXFSZ
can end the stub before Python ignores it, and SIGTERM, SIGINT or
SIGHUP can end it before its source ignores it if the test process
does not ignore it.

The stub's source is a constant, GROUP_STUB. The stub first reads its
own end with float from a file, own_end, that the check writes with
str, so a plain int or float passed as own_end reaches the stub only
as a number; a text that float does not take raises before the stub
opens either FIFO, and the check fails.

The test patches client.wait_child to hold that first wait. An
exception of class Exception, or of a subclass of it, that the
patched wait raises becomes an unavailable verdict in the client, and
the check fails at its reason; any other exception it raises, such as
KeyboardInterrupt, passes through the client and the check.

New tests run the check against a client that kills only the leader,
one that sends SIGTERM to the group, and a client whose group kill
raises KeyboardInterrupt, and assert that each fails or passes the
interrupt through and that the group ends within 5 seconds after it.
Another runs it against a stub whose own end falls inside the check
and asserts that it fails at the own-end assertion, another asserts
that a stub started after the release exits at once, and another
asserts that an end of file seen after its deadline is not taken. A
tripwire test asserts that the only bindings of check_group_kill,
end_of_file and stub in the test file's syntax are 1 def statement
for each, counting async def, class and import statements, every kind
of assignment to a name or an attribute, a lambda so assigned among
them, deletions, targets, parameters and keyword arguments, but not a
name given as a string; that, however it was bound, BoundsTest, each
class derived from it when the test runs and each class in their
method resolution orders hold no other entry with those names, that
BoundsTest's 2 entries and the module's end_of_file are the functions
their def statements made, judged by qualified name and first line,
and that the test's instance has no such attribute of its own; that
the stub makes its pinned calls in order; and that no name in
SIGNAL_NAMES, a list of example names through which Python code sends
a signal, appears in the check, its helpers or the stub, so a direct
os.kill there fails it. Another test has a case for each form of
binding stub that the first 2 of those assertions see, and for 1 that
they miss. The group-kill test asserts nothing about the client's
reap; its docstring names the 2 tests that do.

Unchanged from main: the 1 second timeout, the reason string, the
real wait, kill and reap, and a 10 second window for the group to end
after the client returns.

Reduced coverage, which landing this change accepts: the test has no
allowlist of the check's callees, no pin of the calls that start a
process with their arguments, no type test of check and own_end, no
check that they are not rebound, no check of the stub's calls for
example values of own_end, and no test that a caller's value runs no
code of its own.

Residual: the tripwire's name scan misses every route to a signal
other than a name in SIGNAL_NAMES in the functions it reads, and such
an edit passes the tripwire unless it also changes the stub's calls,
which the pin rejects, or binds check_group_kill, end_of_file or stub
in a way its first 2 assertions reject. Those 2 assertions miss a
change to what self.stub finds without such an entry or attribute,
such as a __getattribute__ method or an assignment to self.__class__;
a class derived from BoundsTest that does not exist when the test
runs; an attribute on an instance other than the test's; a
replacement with the same qualified name and first line; a binding by
a name given as a string anywhere else; and a change made after the
test runs or undone before it. Passes of the name scan, examples, not
a complete list: in the check, getattr(os, "kill") with a literal name,
getattr with a computed name, such as getattr(os, "ki" + "ll"),
os.__dict__["kill"], vars(os)["kill"] and a shell kill through
os.system; a value a caller passes, such as the witness, which the
check calls; a method of self that a subclass overrides, such as
assertLess; a module global or builtin that a caller rebinds, such as
GROUP_STUB, or a function of os or the client, as the tests rebind
os.killpg; the body of a decorator; and the code outside those
functions, the client and the standard library. A value of check or
own_end with methods of its own runs them in the test, and str of
own_end runs before the check reads GROUP_STUB, so a method of
own_end can change the stub's source.

A stub process that the release finds before its first read of
lifeline outlives the release by the rest of its start-up. While the
test process is alive but neither closes lifeline nor ends, as when
it is stopped, each stub process lives its start-up plus 90 seconds.
A client whose real wait gives up early by less than the time the
gate's 2 clock reads and the call add passes; the call's share
includes the wait's overrun past its own deadline, which the code
does not bound, so the host sets the margin.

A process that inherits the write end of lifeline and outlives the
test would keep the stub alive up to its own end; only a fork without
exec in the test process could do that. A stub process that closed
its copy of alive before it ended would hide from the check; only an
altered stub could do that. A process that SIGKILL cannot end keeps
alive open and fails the check. A leader that has not ended within
the 5 second reap grace of the finally clause, or one left when the
test process ends without unwinding, stays unreaped until Python's
own collection of finished children or the process that adopts it
reaps it; while it is still running, it holds its descriptors, the
write end of alive among them. No signal ends the stub while it
ignores or blocks that signal; the signals that can end it before it
ignores them are stated above. Examples of a signal that ends it
early, not a complete list: SIGKILL, and SIGUSR1 when the test
neither ignores nor blocks SIGUSR1. A correct client still fails if
the child is not ready within 60 seconds. The design needs FIFOs,
select on them and the Linux behaviour that a FIFO reader opened
while a writer exists sees end of file when the last writer closes.
This message states the behaviour on Linux; for other platforms and
for the Python 3.9 floor it is not established.

  the Pull request text gate.
